DECK: Discipleship Experience (Section 2) Soteriology II

Q1. Isaiah 32:17 is used to show the result of righteousness in the life of a believer. What does it produce?
A. Boldness and authority
B. Peace, quietness, and assurance forever
C. Spiritual gifts and power
D. Holiness through personal effort
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: Isaiah 32:17 is quoted as saying righteousness produces peace, quietness, and assurance.
REF: ASSURANCE – Celebration Church International - LMS.mp4 — [00:16]–[01:14] (approximate range)

Q2. Which statement best describes propitiation as taught in the lesson?
A. Christ's death satisfied the demands of God's justice.
B. Christ's resurrection replaced His sacrifice.
C. God overlooked humanity's sin.
D. Believers now satisfy God's justice through obedience.
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: Christ’s redemptive work appeased God’s justice; the lesson describes propitiation as satisfaction.
REF: PROPITIATION – Celebration Church International - LMS.mp4 — [00:16]–[01:13] (approximate range)

Q3. The teaching describes reconciliation as God's work through Christ to:
A. reward righteous living.
B. remove the hostility between God and humanity.
C. restore Israel's kingdom.
D. unite all nations politically.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: Reconciliation is described as Christ’s work removing the hostility between God and humanity.
REF: ATONEMENT – Celebration Church International - LMS.mp4 — [02:09]–[04:11] (approximate range)

Q4. What does it mean to redeem someone?
A. Restore a broken relationship.
B. Ignore an offence.
C. Free someone from bondage by paying a ransom.
D. Remove every earthly consequence of sin.
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: To redeem is to free someone from bondage by paying ransom.
REF: REDEMPTION – Celebration Church International - LMS.mp4 — [04:49]–[05:50] (approximate range)

Q5. According to the teaching, why are people "without excuse" before God?
A. They all possess the written Law.
B. Creation reveals the existence of God.
C. Every person has heard the gospel.
D. Every nation received the prophets.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The lesson says creation makes God’s existence knowable and therefore leaves people without excuse.
REF: THOSE WHO NEVER HEARD THE GOSPEL – Celebration Church International - LMS.mp4 — [05:42]–[06:36] (approximate range)

Q6. Believers sometimes struggle with assurance because:
A. God deliberately withholds assurance.
B. They are conditioned to think acceptance must always be earned.
C. Salvation depends on daily performance.
D. Faith naturally produces uncertainty.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The lesson says believers may doubt assurance because they are conditioned to think in terms of what must be earned.
REF: ASSURANCE – Celebration Church International - LMS.mp4 — [02:15]–[03:32] (approximate range)

Q7. The comparison between Noah's ark and the blood of Jesus illustrates that:
A. Christ's atoning work provides the covering that secures believers.
B. Noah earned God's favour through obedience.
C. Judgment is greater under grace.
D. The ark represents heaven.
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: The lesson compares the ark’s protective covering with the covering provided by Jesus’ blood.
REF: ATONEMENT – Celebration Church International - LMS.mp4 — [05:04]–[07:03] (approximate range)

Q8. Which responsibility was specifically associated with a kinsman-redeemer?
A. Leading Israel in worship.
B. Buying back a relative's inheritance.
C. Interpreting the Law.
D. Serving as high priest.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: A kinsman-redeemer could buy back land or inheritance sold because of poverty.
REF: REDEMPTION – Celebration Church International - LMS.mp4 — [00:55]–[01:53] (approximate range)

Q9. Why was Cain mentioned in the teaching?
A. To explain the beginning of sacrifice.
B. To show people instinctively recognize wrongdoing.
C. To introduce God's covenant.
D. To explain the origin of death.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: Cain is used to illustrate that people can recognize wrongdoing without a specific written command.
REF: THOSE WHO NEVER HEARD THE GOSPEL – Celebration Church International - LMS.mp4 — [02:12]–[03:07] (approximate range)

Q10. Paul expressed confidence that God would:
A. prevent believers from facing trials.
B. complete the work He began in believers.
C. remove every weakness immediately.
D. reward only mature Christians.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The lesson quotes Philippians 1:6 as Paul’s confidence that God will complete the good work He began in believers.
REF: ASSURANCE – Celebration Church International - LMS.mp4 — [03:32]–[04:29] (approximate range)

Q11. Propitiation is best understood as:
A. regaining favour where favour had been lost.
B. becoming spiritually mature.
C. earning God's acceptance.
D. receiving spiritual gifts.
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: The lesson explains propitiation as appeasement or satisfaction and describes it as regaining favor where it was lost.
REF: PROPITIATION – Celebration Church International - LMS.mp4 — [00:16]–[01:13] (approximate range)

Q12. Who initiated humanity's reconciliation with God?
A. Humanity
B. The Church
C. God
D. The Prophets
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: The lesson explicitly identifies God as the initiator of reconciliation.
REF: ATONEMENT – Celebration Church International - LMS.mp4 — [08:05]–[08:56] (approximate range)

Q13. Why does redemption and forgiveness go hand in hand?
A. Forgiveness came at the cost of Christ's blood.
B. Forgiveness replaced redemption.
C. Redemption only applies to Israel.
D. Forgiveness is earned through obedience.
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: The lesson connects redemption and forgiveness, saying forgiveness came at the cost of Christ’s blood.
REF: REDEMPTION – Celebration Church International - LMS.mp4 — [06:49]–[07:57] (approximate range)

Q14. Romans 2 teaches that even those without God's written law possess:
A. complete knowledge of salvation.
B. an instinctive awareness of right and wrong.
C. perfect obedience.
D. the Abrahamic covenant.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The lesson says people without the written law still have an instinctive moral awareness.
REF: THOSE WHO NEVER HEARD THE GOSPEL – Celebration Church International - LMS.mp4 — [01:09]–[02:12] (approximate range)

Q15. The illustration of protecting a candle from the wind emphasizes:
A. self-preservation.
B. perseverance through discipline.
C. the Holy Spirit's preserving work.
D. the importance of church leadership.
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: The candle illustration describes the Holy Spirit preserving believers.
REF: ASSURANCE – Celebration Church International - LMS.mp4 — [06:14]–[07:19] (approximate range)

Q16. Isaiah 53:11 supports propitiation by stating that the Lord would:
A. remember sin forever.
B. see the suffering of His Servant and be satisfied.
C. establish a new covenant.
D. judge Israel's enemies.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The lesson connects Isaiah 53:11’s ‘be satisfied’ with propitiation as satisfaction.
REF: PROPITIATION – Celebration Church International - LMS.mp4 — [00:16]–[01:13] (approximate range)

Q17. The Greek word katalaso helps explain reconciliation by emphasizing:
A. an exchange made possible through Christ.
B. forgiveness without sacrifice.
C. moral improvement.
D. religious devotion.
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: The lesson describes reconciliation as involving an exchange made possible through Christ’s substitution.
REF: ATONEMENT – Celebration Church International - LMS.mp4 — [07:03]–[08:05] (approximate range)

Q18. The statement, "The judge is the one who paid the price," highlights that:
A. Christ fully met the requirements needed for believers' freedom.
B. everyone pays for personal sin.
C. justice was cancelled.
D. believers no longer face temptation.
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: The lesson says Christ, who knows the requirements, paid the price in full, freeing believers from guilt.
REF: REDEMPTION – Celebration Church International - LMS.mp4 — [10:40]–[11:29] (approximate range)

Q19. The story of Cornelius illustrates that:
A. good works save.
B. God responds to sincere seekers and brings them further light.
C. evangelism is unnecessary.
D. prayer alone brings salvation.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The Apostle says God responds to those seeking Him and describes God sending Peter to Cornelius with further information.
REF: THOSE WHO NEVER HEARD THE GOSPEL – Celebration Church International - LMS.mp4 — [06:36]–[07:33] and [16:38]–[17:33] (approximate ranges)

Q20. According to Jude 24, believers can be confident because God is able to:
A. make them wealthy.
B. keep them from stumbling.
C. remove all suffering.
D. prevent every temptation.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The lesson quotes Jude 24 as assurance that God is able to keep believers from stumbling.
REF: ASSURANCE – Celebration Church International - LMS.mp4 — [08:07]–[09:14] (approximate range)

Q21. Romans 3:25 teaches that Christ became our propitiation through:
A. His teachings.
B. His blood.
C. His miracles.
D. His resurrection.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The lesson explicitly says Christ was set forth as propitiation by His blood.
REF: PROPITIATION – Celebration Church International - LMS.mp4 — [02:14]–[03:11] (approximate range)

Q22. The Holy Spirit's role in reconciliation includes:
A. replacing Christ's work.
B. applying the benefits of reconciliation to believers.
C. judging unbelievers.
D. establishing the Law.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The lesson identifies the Holy Spirit as the applier of reconciliation.
REF: ATONEMENT – Celebration Church International - LMS.mp4 — [08:05]–[08:56] (approximate range)

Q23. Christ became our kinsman-redeemer by:
A. becoming human.
B. being born into Israel.
C. fulfilling the Law.
D. After completing discipleship classes.
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: The lesson says Christ became human and thereby became our kinsman.
REF: REDEMPTION – Celebration Church International - LMS.mp4 — [03:52]–[04:49] (approximate range)

Q24. What assumption does the teaching challenge about people who have never heard the gospel?
A. That they are automatically innocent before God.
B. That they are all saved.
C. That they lived before Christ.
D. That they rejected the gospel.
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: The lesson challenges the assumption that people are justified simply because they have not heard the gospel.
REF: THOSE WHO NEVER HEARD THE GOSPEL – Celebration Church International - LMS.mp4 — [00:00]–[01:09] (approximate range)

Q25. According to the teaching, assurance is strongest when it is based on:
A. personal consistency.
B. spiritual discipline.
C. God's preserving work.
D. church accountability.
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: The lesson grounds assurance in God and the Spirit’s preserving work rather than in self-confidence.
REF: ASSURANCE – Celebration Church International - LMS.mp4 — [06:14]–[07:19] (approximate range)

Q26. Rahab's example shows that genuine faith is:
A. based on complete theological knowledge.
B. demonstrated through corresponding actions.
C. limited to Israel.
D. always rewarded immediately.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: Rahab’s actions are presented as a demonstration of her faith.
REF: THOSE WHO NEVER HEARD THE GOSPEL – Celebration Church International - LMS.mp4 — [12:40]–[13:39] (approximate range)

Q27. According to the second view presented, people are judged based on:
A. their nationality.
B. the light they received and how they responded to it.
C. the era in which they lived.
D. the number of good works they performed.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The second view is described as judgment according to the information a person received and their response to it.
REF: THOSE WHO NEVER HEARD THE GOSPEL – Celebration Church International - LMS.mp4 — [13:39]–[14:50] (approximate range)

Q28. What enables believers to call God "Abba, Father"?
A. Spiritual maturity.
B. The spirit of adoption received through the Holy Spirit.
C. Faithful church attendance.
D. Keeping the commandments.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The lesson links the Spirit of adoption with believers crying ‘Abba, Father.’
REF: ATONEMENT – Celebration Church International - LMS.mp4 — [08:05]–[08:56] (approximate range)

Q29. One result of Christ's propitiatory work emphasized in the teaching is that believers:
A. stand without guilt before God.
B. no longer need repentance.
C. become incapable of sin.
D. immediately become spiritually mature.
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: The lesson says propitiation means believers stand without guilt before God.
REF: PROPITIATION – Celebration Church International - LMS.mp4 — [03:11]–end of transcript (approximate boundary)

Q30. Which statement best reflects the Apostle's own conclusion regarding those who have never heard the gospel?
A. They are automatically saved.
B. They are automatically condemned.
C. He leans toward the view that God judges people according to the light they have received.
D. Scripture provides no basis for any conclusion.
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: The Apostle says he leans toward the view based on the information a person received and their receptiveness to it.
REF: THOSE WHO NEVER HEARD THE GOSPEL – Celebration Church International - LMS.mp4 — [18:40]–end of transcript (approximate boundary); see also [13:39]–[14:50] (approximate range)
